title: First run: 38 questions with the answer written down first
changed: Ten sql questions where the answer depends on the owner's definition. For example, a 'regular' at Mekong Noodle House is someone with three or more completed orders in three months, while at Ridgeline Coffee it is four or more orders in a month. The vendor's definitions live in [the prompt](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/agent/prompt.py). Each owner's live in a Definitions document beside their policies, which the agent searches and cites like any other section.
Pre-written gold queries for each question.

Fifteen policy questions, including two where the nearest section is the wrong one. Eight proposals that code has to check against the rules. Three questions that must be declined, one about the other restaurant, one that needs no search.

Twenty-four months of data with named menus, food costs, one price per item per channel, a promotion, loyalty rewards, seasonal items and regulars who stop coming, so these questions have answers in the data.
Retrieval threshold 0.50, a number picked from ten captured runs before this set existed.
moved: [sql-05](/evaluation/sql-05) wrong by 6%: a safe query with a time zone slip.
[pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) and [pol-12](/evaluation/pol-12) hidden by the threshold, at 0.28 and 0.47.
[pol-11](/evaluation/pol-11) right answer, short citation label, failed by code.

title: Fifth run: the grader's rule for a not-covered case
changed: Two rules deleted from [the grader](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/evals/grade.py). A question the policies do not cover used to fail if any section was shown or cited. Now it passes when the answer says the policies do not cover it and cites nothing as the rule, and the citations step applies to every policy case.

This changes the test, not the agent. Scored by the new rule, run 2 would be 34 and run 4 would be 38. Run 3 would stay at 35, because that answer said it couldn't find a rule, and my phrase list does not have those words.

title: Regrade: two phrase lists widened, no model run
changed: Two word lists in [the cases](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/evals/cases.json) grew. The health inspections case accepts 'couldn't find' and 'could not find' as ways of saying the policies do not cover it. The campaign case accepts 'you approve', 'you can approve' and 'your approval' as naming the owner, because the owner is the one asking.
The five runs were graded again with today's grader, which also carries the not-covered rule from run 5. Nothing was asked of the model.
result: By today's grader: run 2 is 34, run 3 is 36, run 4 is 38, run 5 is 37.
moved: [pol-05](/evaluation/pol-05) passes in runs 2, 3 and 4. Each answer said the policies do not cover it, in words my list did not have, or cited the near section to say it does not apply.
[pol-11](/evaluation/pol-11) passes in run 5. The answer told the owner 'unless you approve more', which names the owner when the owner is asking.

[pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) is the one failure left in every run but run 4, and the only one about the agent. A word list checks words and a person checks meaning. Twice in five runs the list was missing a wording I should have put in.
next: The hidden section needs a search that matches a word as well as a meaning. Six single-case reps of prompt wording put its score at 0.37 to 0.39 against a 0.40 line. That is code, a different system, and the next experiment.

title: Sixth run: the policy search matches words as well as meaning
changed: [The search](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/policies/search.py) now scores every section two ways. The meaning score is the embedding similarity, as before. The word score is the sum of the rarity of the search's words that appear in the section, within this restaurant's policies, so 'DoorDash' in one section of twenty-five outweighs 'order' in fifteen. The two rankings are merged by rank, and the section whose words match best is shown even when its meaning score is under the threshold. One new column in the policy table, built by Postgres from the section text.
This is a different kind of change from the prompt lines: a new mechanism, with its own tests, and the first run of a new retriever. The threshold, the prompt and the grader did not change.
Before the full run, the hidden-section case was run three times on its own and passed all three, after passing one of six with prompt wording.
moved: [pol-02](/evaluation/pol-02) passed. Its first search showed the Delivery Marketplaces section for its words, with a meaning score of 0.34, and the agent cited it.

Recall 93% to 100%. Precision 29% to 28%: 50 sections shown across 38 searches against 45 in run 5. Five were shown for their words alone. One was the section this change was for. The other four were the same section every time, the scope preamble of the house policy, which shares common words with most questions and which the agent set aside each time.
Nothing else moved.
next: Nothing is failing. The next run is a different model, or a different set of questions, and either one is a new experiment.

title: Seventh run: one question added, and nothing else
changed: A new sql case, sql-11: how many catering orders in October. The owner's reading is an order with an item from the Catering category on the menu. Nothing on the order itself says catering, no channel, no label, no discount. The question came from asking the live agent questions with a second plausible reading, after the set had gone to 38 of 38.
No change to the prompt, the search, the threshold or the grader. The run shows the set with the new case before anything is done about it.
moved: [sql-11](/evaluation/sql-11) failed, as it had three times in ad hoc asks. The agent searched the order's source label and discount name for the word catering, found nothing, and said the data has no way to identify a catering order. It never looked at the menu categories, which are in its prompt.
Nothing else moved.
next: A fix for the empty result read as a fact. The two misses of this shape so far, this one and a question about a day with no data, both turned zero rows into a claim about the restaurant.

title: Eighth run: the prompt says a word may be a menu category, and the catering question moves to a finished month
changed: Four lines in [the prompt](https://github.com/rostgoat/restaurant-ops-agent/blob/main/api/app/agent/prompt.py), under Queries: a word in the question may be the name of a menu category or item, check the categories and items tables for it before saying the data cannot identify something, and an empty search proves only that the word is not where you looked.

The case itself was wrong. It asked about October, and the eval's clock is frozen at 24 October, so the agent rightly counted to the 24th while my gold counted to the end of the data. It now asks about September, a finished month, with the gold at 22.

Before the full run, three single-case reps each way on the September wording. Without the line, two of three found the menu. With the line, three of three. On the October wording the day before, none of three had.
moved: [sql-11](/evaluation/sql-11) passed. The agent listed the Catering category's six items first, then counted completed September orders that include one.
Nothing else moved. Precision 28% to 30%.
next: Two changes in one run, and the second was a correction to the test, so the single-case reps are the evidence that the line did the work. The third kind of wrong, a cited section that does not support the answer, still has no case.
